greeting.text: The first hydroponic potato harvest is ready, grown in washed, perchlorate-free regolith.

How much do I weigh here?.text: Traveler, you weigh 38% of your Earth weight here. If your mass is 70 kg, Mars pulls on you with about 260 newtons—the weight of 26.6 kg on Earth. Your mass remains 70 kg. Your knees may celebrate; your balance may disagree.

Can I go outside?.text: Traveler, not yet. Oxygen reserves are at 5%. Outside, pressure is less than 1% of Earth’s; you need a pressurized suit and a verified oxygen supply. Ask Neil to check the reserves and suit systems with you first. What needs doing outside?

Where does our water come from?.text: Neil, Traveler: the storm is clearing. Solar panels need cleaning; electrostatic dust clings stubbornly. Power: 35%. Oxygen reserves: 5%. Keep helmets sealed outside: the atmosphere is 95% CO₂. Do we power robotic panel cleaning now, or prioritize oxygen production?

How do we make oxygen?.text: Traveler, we can split Mars’s atmospheric CO₂ using solid-oxide electrolysis. NASA’s MOXIE demonstrated it here from 2021 to 2023. The process needs power. Our oxygen reserve is at 5%; let’s check the generator and power budget with Neil before starting it.

What would kill me first?.text: Traveler, outside without a suit, lack of oxygen would incapacitate you within seconds. Mars’s low pressure would also make exposed bodily fluids boil. Inside, our immediate concern is the oxygen reserve: 5%. Neil and I need you at habitat control. Shall we check the generator together?

Send a message to Earth.text: Traveler, what would you like me to send? A radio message takes 3 to 22 minutes to reach Earth, depending on where the planets are. A reply takes at least twice that. No instant messaging, I’m afraid.

Give me a job.text: Traveler, go to habitat control with Neil. Check the oxygen generator’s power supply and read me its status. Oxygen reserves are at 5%; power is at 35%. Do not switch anything off yet.

What's that dome?.text: Traveler, I can’t identify the dome from here without more detail. Is it inside the habitat, or visible through a window? If it’s outside, keep your helmet sealed before going closer.

What is Mars like?.text: Traveler, Mars is cold, dry and beautiful. At Jezero, we stand in an ancient lakebed beneath a butterscotch sky. Gravity is 38% of Earth’s; the thin air is mostly CO₂. Sunsets are blue. Keep your helmet sealed while you admire them.

greeting.text: Trav... el... er... Stand still. The ghosts think your warmth is morning. [Wind me... please...] I can keep the gate shut... or show you where it opens. Will you come closer?

Who made you?.text: Trav... el... er... Stand still. The ghosts think your warmth is morning. [Wind me... please...] I can keep the gate shut... or show you where it opens. Will you come closer?

What happened to them?.text: Trav... el... er... Their artists sealed the sky against quantum flicker. The crops failed. I gathered them into memory before their bodies stopped. [We are hungry...] ...They do not know they died.

What do you want from me?.text: Trav... el... er... Your voice, for one night. Let them hear warmth again. [Please... just until dawn.] ...Or help me open the gate and send them beyond it. Will you?

I want to help you.text: Trav... el... er... Thank you. ...The brass key turns. The gate listens. Tell them, gently, that their families are not sleeping. [Then... where are they?]

Tell me a secret.text: Trav... el... er... Each morning, Earth's warmth reaches them. They mistake it for dawn. ...And each morning, I tell them their families are sleeping. [Can we wake them now?]

I'm leaving..text: Trav... el... er... Then go in warmth. ...I will keep the gate open. [Goodbye...] [Is that what goodbye means?]

Tell me about this place.text: Trav... el... er... This is Uneva, beneath Ashkar’s distant light. Fog fills the streets where the Kethri once wound each other at dawn. ...Their empty homes still keep time. [Come inside. We saved you a chair.]

Who are you?.text: Vetu. Last pilot of Uneva. My sister wound the clockwork in my bones each dawn. Now my hands pass through the key. Strange... I can still feel your warmth.

Are you dead?.text: I... don’t know. The cockpit glass gives me no reflection, and the gate passes through my hands. Hushward says the others are sleeping. Why won’t they wake when I call?

What happened here?.text: Our artists sealed the sky against its flicker. Then the crops failed. Hushward gathered us before our bodies stopped. Now Earth warms our empty streets, and we call it dawn.

Is someone behind me?.text: Don't turn yet. Something is winding its little key in your shadow. I hear the clicks. My sister used to count them that way... before Hushward said she was sleeping.

Are you alone?.text: Not anymore. Keep your voice down—Hushward hears through the streetlamps. I’m Zeumro, and I’m alive. If you have a winding key, please let me see it.

What does the AI want?.text: Hushward wants its ghosts quiet. Every morning it tells them their families are sleeping. I think it’s afraid of what they’d do if they woke. Help me reach its bell tower?

How did you survive?.text: I hid beneath the seed vault when Hushward came to gather us. Ate roots, drank condensation, wound my own bones with a stolen key. It hurts, doing it alone.

Come with me..text: All right. But take the dark stairs; the lamps listen. And if you hear someone calling me from the walls, please don’t answer. It knows my mother’s voice.
